q8.label: 8-bit model · text encoder on the GPU

q8_low_vram.label: 8-bit model · loaded one part at a time

sources.locked: ai-toolkit extensions_built_in/diffusion_models/ui.tsx (moss_image:base; moss_image arrived in ai-toolkit 0.13.27, Base and the fresh-cache tokenizer fix in 0.13.28, which this recipe needs); moss_image/moss_image.py, which reads the Base transformer as Comfy-Org/MOSS-Image's moss_image_base_bf16.safetensors (byte-identical to the vendor shards), the Qwen3.5-9B text encoder from Comfy-Org/Qwen3.5 and the shared FLUX.2 VAE. The arch tag is stripped by ai-toolkit; the Base checkpoint comes from name_or_path. uncond_skip_layers [22] is the vendor's sampling default, and the LoRA is kept off block 22 so the skipped-block contrast stays the base model's, as ai-toolkit's UI does. Latents are cached, as for Krea 2, where encoding every step was measured at 5 GB above training
sources.divisibility: moss_image.py get_bucket_divisibility: 16 (the VAE's 8x and the 2x2 packing)
sources.defaults: ai-toolkit UI defaults for moss_image:base (timestep shift; the trainer's scheduler shift is 5, the vendor's)
sources.preview.base: OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-Base model card: 50 steps at CFG 3, shift 5, block 22 skipped on the negative branch, 1024 x 1024; the vendor's user guide says Base needs at least 50 steps. Previews use 30 steps, ai-toolkit's own default for the arch, to keep a preview round short
sources.subject: heuristic, as for Z-Image Turbo: ai-toolkit's own caption dropout default is 0.0; content_or_style per jobs/process/BaseSDTrainProcess.py
sources.effort: heuristic, as for Chroma1 Base: the vendor's user guide gives no LoRA steps or learning rate, so the step ranges are Z-Image Turbo's and the learning rates Krea 2's
sources.fit: the 8-bit profiles quantise with qfloat8, for which ai-toolkit picks the bf16 text encoder and transformer files and quantises them itself; its UI default, convrot8, is not a qtype PixlStash offers. ai-toolkit turns qfloat8 into float8 when layers are offloaded
sources.hardware_profiles: derived from moss_image.py's load order and the weights, never run here: a 5.1B transformer (10.2 GB bf16, about 5.3 GB qfloat8 with its full-precision exclusions), the Qwen3.5-9B text encoder without its vision tower (18.4 GB bf16, about 10 GB qfloat8, of which 2 GB is the token embedding the quantiser leaves in bf16), a 0.3 GB VAE, about 0.7 GB of LoRA, gradients and 8-bit Adam at rank 32, about 2.2 GB of activations at 1024 and about 1 GB to encode a picture's latents; each vram_mb calibrated like every untested seed here: the derived peak plus 0.6 GB of CUDA context, x1.08 (what Krea 2's derivation missed against its measurement) and x1.1 (the margin a measured peak is admitted with). The text encoder is larger than the transformer, so wherever it reaches the GPU it sets the peak
sources.hardware_profiles.q8.vram_mb: derived: the quantised transformer and text encoder resident, plus VAE, LoRA state and activations, 18.5 GB before calibration
sources.hardware_profiles.q8_cached.vram_mb: derived: both quantised models are on the GPU while captions and latents are encoded, 16.6 GB before calibration; ai-toolkit unloads the text encoder afterwards, so training's 8.5 GB is lower
sources.hardware_profiles.q8_low_vram.vram_mb: derived: low_vram keeps both models in RAM until each is needed; the peak is the 10 GB quantised text encoder encoding captions beside the VAE, 11.3 GB before calibration
sources.hardware_profiles.q8_offload.vram_mb: derived: 60% of both quantised models' layers in RAM, as measured worthwhile on Krea 2's transformer. The text encoder is offloaded too, unlike Klein's, because here it sets the peak: caption encoding with 40% of its layers and its embedding on the GPU, 6.5 GB before calibration, above training's 5.3 GB
sources.hardware_profiles.bf16_cached.vram_mb: derived: the 18.4 GB bf16 text encoder encoding captions sets the peak, 19.7 GB before calibration; low_vram keeps it off the GPU while the 10.2 GB bf16 transformer trains (13.4 GB)
sources.hardware_profiles.*.max_rank, max_batch: the rank and batch size the VRAM figures were derived at
sources.hardware_profiles.*.ram_mb: derived: the bf16 transformer state dict and the 19.3 GB bf16 text-encoder file, 29.5 GB, in RAM together while they are quantised or parked, x1.3 for what Krea 2's RAM derivation missed against its resident-memory measurement, and x1.1 margin
